what_happened: Layout 10 (corner with toaster), bar-handle top drawer at straw x=0.93. 0-240 approach. 247-315 the gripper hooked the long horizontal bar handle with half-open fingers (width 0.05-0.068; the bar lies across the finger axis, it is not between the fingers) and pulled: drawer 0.15 (272) -> 0.37 (288) -> 0.62 (304) -> 0.853 at 320, where it stopped. The fingers closed on air at 308-320 as the handle slipped out, and stayed closed (width ~0.001) for the rest of the episode. The policy never came back to the drawer (drawer touch only 247-315). 480-780 it hovered above the half-open drawer with the straw visible but never descended (closest eef-to-straw 0.30 m); from ~840 it wandered over the counter. Straw never touched; drawer 0.853 at the end.
causal_chain: handle hooked, not grasped (247) -> handle slipped off at 0.853 (320; needs 0.95, ~47% of physical travel) -> fingers closed on air and never reopened -> hovered over the straw with a closed gripper 480-780 -> wandered until timeout (1700)
self_recovery: none: no second pull and no attempt at the straw (fingers stayed closed).
official_criterion_notes: Drawer value = slide joint / (0.55 x drawer depth), so fully open reads ~1.82 and the 0.95 threshold is ~52% of the physical travel; the composite task's own _check_success does not check the drawer at all (only straw-cup contact within 0.5 m + gripper far). At 0.853 the straw was visible in the drawer, so the drawer was probably open enough for the pick; the policy, not the opening, ended the episode.
uncertain_about: Whether the policy would have reached the straw at this opening if it had reopened the fingers.
